$comment: Shared deep-loop offer cases. Read by the TypeScript offer-gate test and the Python advisor test, so the native gate and the Python fallback agree on which prompts ask for a loop run, which complain about a stuck run and which write about the loop. asksForLoopRun is the full gate, after the past-run, stuck-run, write-about and question exceptions. typedReviewKept, where present, says whether a typed /deep:review keeps its command at the attachCommand layer in TypeScript, on a single review route and before the typed-command override, so a stuck-run complaint there answers with the doctor. servedReviewKept, present on every typedReviewKept case, says whether the served head carries /deep:review: attachTypedCommand over the attachCommand result in TypeScript, which the handler serving test confirms on the real advisor_recommend head, and in Python the run row the gate keeps and analyze_request serves, because the fallback gates the run rows before the command-bridge rename and has no separate typed layer. The two differ only where a typed command meets a stuck-run complaint, where the reader's typed command stays on the served head. typedRunsKept, where present, lists the /deep:* commands a prompt that types more than one command keeps at the gate layer: attachCommand on a single route of that command's mode in TypeScript, and the run rows the Python gate keeps, so one typed command never hides another. It pins the gate only, because another command such as /create:changelog can win the served head. doctorWithheld, where present, says whether a prompt loses /doctor:deep-loop: attachCommand on a single review route and the fused doctor row after the scorer's doctor and no-edit withholds in TypeScript, and the doctor row in the Python gate. A naming that refuses or asks about the doctor loses the row even when the reader typed it, while a bare naming on a stuck run keeps it, so the rows cover both a stuck-run complaint and a question about the command. A refusal verb lead, such as skip or avoid, stops at a conjunction, so 'skip it and deep review the parser' asks for the run. servedRun, where present, says which deep-loop run the ask serves: the native deferred route offers that mode's command and no other, and the Python gate keeps that mode's run row and no other. "none" answers a prompt that names no single mode, which is an ask for both modes at once or for the loop's own name with no mode at all; neither copy then serves a run, the native route offering no command and the fallback keeping no run row, so the reader picks the mode. The column carries one of those three words and never null, because a null cannot tell an ask that serves no run from one that serves both.
